gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-fs-quicksand: Quicksand rounds everything off, its bulb-shaped lowercase finishing in terminals that stop well short of the stem. Quicksand would carry a whole page gently, since Rounded Elegance already speaks in the same thin, warm line.
gen-dafont-rounded-elegance-switzer: Switzer holds its wire-like letterforms apart, with c tips that never drift toward touching, while Rounded Elegance crowds its monoline characters almost into overlap. One is snug and inviting, the other crisp.
gen-dafont-sansumi-fs-asap: Sansumi spaces its rod-like letters wide apart, each stroke flat and uncarved, with a first capital barely rising above the rest. Asap follows with open arcs and a body height close to its capitals; a modest heading size lets that tracking breathe.
gen-dafont-sansumi-fs-epilogue: Approachable curves give Epilogue a loose, unclamped feel, stubby ascender tips and all. Epilogue keeps a wire-thin skeleton, while Sansumi, with its wide-tracked geometric rods, earns its keep in large, brief headings.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-asap: Stilu draws curves and straights at the same line width, with terminals that never close in, which gives it a luxurious hush. Asap stays readable beside it.
gen-dafont-stilu-fs-epilogue: Epilogue reads loose and contemporary, its curvy wire-thin letters feeling unclamped on the page. And Stilu, with bulb-shaped lowercase and open terminals, is close enough in build that sizes can match without any fuss.
gen-dafont-stilu-switzer: Stilu keeps one line width through every curve and straight, its glass-bulb bowls never closing in at the terminals. Switzer carries that over into running text, with wire-like letters and a high waist line that keep a long page feeling light.
gen-dafont-vcr-osd-mono-general-sans: Pure lo-fi, camcorder-menu energy, with VCR OSD Mono's towering x-height and fixed-width code letters. And General Sans smooths it over, its steady pen pressure and unobstructed bends making the retro-tech edge feel friendlier.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-hoover: Verve packs its letters tight, bowls nearly sealed and strokes swinging from thick to hairline. Hoover opens up the e's eye and trims its ascenders, so a long page feels refined and sturdy beside it.
gen-dafont-verve-fs-quicksand: Hairline against heavy, that is Verve, bowls nearly shut and spacing trimmed to a sliver. But Quicksand is spaghetti-like and open, so give it a little extra size to let those same-width strokes hold up.
